summary: Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna and Visva-Bharati universities. He served as professor at Utkal University (~1960–1975) and held posts at Gangadhar Meher University, Visva-Bharati, Ravenshaw College, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit University.

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Georgetown University, he held posts at the University of Chicago (~1963–1980) and Harvard University (~1980–2003), where he was professor and taught Marylin Martin Rhie.
Prapod Assavavirulhakarn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic posts include positions at Chulalongkorn University (attested 1998) and Ryukoku University (attested 2014).
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed a PhD at the University of Mysore (attested 2014).
Pratap Kumar Penumala (born 1952) works in religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a visiting professor at Colorado College.

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) is an Indology, Tibetology, and art history scholar. He held long-term posts at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1970–1995, attested 2007) and served at the Art Institute of Chicago in 1995.

Prayoon Mererk (born 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Oslo and Mainz, taught at Mainz, worked at Columbia, and served as Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies at Harvard (~1991–2014).

Projit Bihari Mukharji works in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at Presidency, JNU, and SOAS. He held posts at Newcastle, McMaster, Ashoka, and the University of Pennsylvania (~2013–2022), where he was Professor of History of Science.

Pulinbihari Chakravarti was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. In 1951, he was attested as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society.

Purushottama Bilimoria is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at La Trobe. He has held posts at Deakin, Melbourne, UC Berkeley, Stony Brook, and Columbia, and he taught Colin Leslie Dean.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London in 2014. She also served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Pál Miklós (1927–2002) was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1945–1950) and Peking University (~1950–1954), and he taught Lilla Russell-Smith.

Péter-Dániel Szántó is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Alexis Sanderson at Balliol College and Eötvös Loránd University. He has held positions at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Fudan University, the University of Bristol (MA, 2004), and the University of Washington (PhD, 2015), where she studied under Collett Cox.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed doctoral studies under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. He held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and researched at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied under Kang Youwei (~1890–1898), attended National Tsing Hua University, and held a post at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929).

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg, and served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022), where she taught Shaoyong Ye.

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) studied at Qinghai Normal, Qinghai Nationalities, and Minzu universities. Specializing in Tibetology and history, he taught Penghao Sun and held posts at Minzu, Southwest Minzu, and the China Tibetology Research Center (~1986–2022).
Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He has held professorships at Peking University (attested 2004) and The Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
